there are three types of energy models for Cloud applications, namely the energy-aware model, the energy-aware resource provisioning model, and the energy-aware resource allocation model.

“the energy consumption of Cloud computing applications can be influenced by multiple environmental factors and workload factors, and the impacts of these factors are often complicated, with trade-offs and even disputes.”

there are 76 relevant studies and 30 different models, and the energy consumption is affected by 18 environmental factors (e.g., virtualization overhead, data transmission) and 12 workload characteristics (e.g., CPU utilization, memory usage).

modeling energy consumption of Cloud application and the trade-off debates, and provides a systematic survey of current research efforts, which can serve as a valuable guide for future research and practice.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in order to achieve energy efficiency in Cloud computing, it is necessary to take a holistic perspective that considers the impacts of all the environmental and workload factors.
there is no single model that can cover all aspects of Cloud application energy consumption.
there are no universal and perfect models, and that there is a long way to go to achieve this goal in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modeling efforts have been mainly focused on the runtime execution environment, and the deployment environment has been less investigated.
the existing models have been developed in a fragmented manner.
the existing models are mainly designed for specific purposes and scenarios, and there is no single model that can be applied universally.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the energy consumption of a Cloud application is not only a function of its workload, but is also determined by a number of other environmental factors, such as the underlying hardware architecture, virtualization technology, and the deployment environment.
the modeling approach has the potential to help understand and optimize application energy consumption, but the modeling results should be interpreted with caution.

, to achieve a better balance between accuracy, applicability, and simplicity of the model, the modelers have to carefully consider the purpose, application characteristics, and the environment in which they want to apply the model.
